assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of firm heterogeneity and selection that changed modern trade theory and empirical work on trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical framework; Helpman and Redding made major connected theoretical and quantitative contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been deeply incorporated into trade research and policy analysis over two decades.
uncertainties: The breadth of subsequent contributors makes the precise three-person attribution contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work supplied durable models of liquidity, dealer intermediation, search, and funding conditions with major implications for asset pricing and financial stability.
assessment.attribution: Duffie and Pedersen are especially central across the connected literature, with Garleanu a major contributor to its asset-market foundations.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested, widely used, and gained added relevance through financial-market disruptions.
uncertainties: The contribution overlaps with broader liquidity and macro-finance literatures involving additional researchers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible analysis of panel data with persistence, fixed effects, and endogenous regressors broadly feasible.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond provided the seminal estimator, while Blundell was central to the system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These methods are longstanding standards across applied economics, with their limitations now well understood.
uncertainties: The field's extensive use also reflects later diagnostic and implementation work beyond the proposed laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-based amplification mechanism gave macroeconomics a powerful explanation of how asset prices and credit constraints intensify cycles.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clearest originators of the core collateral-cycle mechanism.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large subsequent literature and proved highly influential in interpreting financial crises.
uncertainties: Its relation to the broader financial-accelerator literature complicates the boundary of credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established management practices as measurable organizational capital and a consequential source of productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen developed the central measurement and empirical agenda; Sadun made important contributions to its extension and organizational interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated across settings and have shaped research on firms, productivity, and policy.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation and the generality of surveyed management measures remain active research questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance theory with administrative and market data transformed measurement of adverse selection and welfare in insurance markets.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are central empirical innovators, while Salanie made foundational theoretical and econometric contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and influential across health, auto, and other insurance applications.
uncertainties: The relevant body of work is broad, with several other important contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation program made firm-level distortions a central quantitative explanation for productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow supplied the influential empirical-quantitative benchmark; Restuccia made major foundational contributions to the broader framework.
assessment.maturity: It has generated extensive measurement, theoretical, and policy research across countries and sectors.
uncertainties: Measured wedges can reflect forces other than allocative distortions, limiting direct policy interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression created a broadly useful approach for studying heterogeneous conditional distributions rather than only mean effects.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett originated the defining method and are its unambiguous principal credit holders.
assessment.maturity: The method is longstanding, technically developed, and widely deployed throughout economics and adjacent fields.
uncertainties: Its extraordinary methodological importance may be viewed as less unified with a single substantive economic discovery.
